response.goal: Fix the n8n workflow so the full CSV file of about 5,000 rows lands in Google Sheets every night without failing due to rate limits, complete with retries and a Slack notification if it still fails.

plan.step: Analyze existing n8n workflow and identify the exact Google Sheets node failure point causing the 429 Too Many Requests error.
Redesign the data ingestion logic to handle batching, rate limiting, and chunking for the 5,000 rows.
Implement robust error handling with automated retries and Slack notification alerts upon persistent failure.
Test the updated workflow end-to-end with the full dataset and verify successful execution.

milestones.name: Audit and Redesign
milestones.deliverable: Updated n8n workflow structure with batching logic to avoid Google Sheets API rate limits.

milestones.name: Testing and Deployment
milestones.deliverable: Fully tested workflow deployed with retries and Slack alerts configured.

risks.risk: Google Sheets API rate limits (429) may still occur if batch sizes are set too high.
risks.mitigation: Implement appropriate chunking and delay intervals between batch requests within n8n.

risks.risk: Missing credentials or webhook access for Slack integration.
risks.mitigation: Confirm client access and permissions for both Google Sheets and Slack prior to starting.

questions: What is the current batch size or pagination setting in the failing n8n Google Sheets node?
Which Slack channel or webhook URL should the failure notification messages be sent to?
assumptions: The client will provide temporary access to the existing n8n instance and relevant API credentials.
The fixed price budget of $250 is fully aligned with the scope of auditing and fixing this single workflow.
